I am an 85-year-old woman in Mwanza, and this small plot of 0.36 hectares is all I have. I grow cassava intercropped with some beans and sweet potato because these crops feed my household and do not fail even when the rains are not generous. At my age, I cannot carry heavy bags of fertilizer from the market, and these crops grow well enough with the compost and ash I put from the kitchen. I save my little money for food and medicine, not for chemicals or hired help, though I may pay a young neighbor for a few days when the soil is hard and my back is too weak for the hoe.
